editorial.title: Corporate Website vs Landing Page: Which Does Your Business Need?
editorial.excerpt: Learn the practical difference between a corporate website and a landing page, when to use each, and how to choose based on audience, traffic, conversion, and content needs.
keyTakeaways: A landing page concentrates attention around a specific offer, audience, campaign, or action.
A corporate website provides a broader information architecture for people researching the business.
The right choice depends on where visitors come from and what they need to know before acting.
A B2B buyer may need services, capabilities, case studies, company information, proof, and contact options before starting a conversation.
A corporate site can contain landing pages, so the choice does not always have to be either-or.
Information architecture should reduce uncertainty: visitors should know what the company does, whether it is credible, and what to do next.
